title: Runtime: load quantization profile artifacts, apply mode, and emit observability signals
author: Noah Patel
release_notes:
- Runtime now consumes resolved quantization profile selection metadata and deterministically applies an approved profile when enabled.
- Added metrics/log annotations for quantization profile applied/fallback/disabled outcomes and artifact load/cache behavior.
body: Summary: This PR wires the serving runtime to (1) consume the resolved quantization profile reference from routing metadata, (2) fetch and validate the corresponding profile metadata + artifacts from the model registry, (3) apply quantization mode deterministically for the request/model shard, and (4) emit metrics + structured events so rollouts can be observed and debugged. Motivation: The Quantization Profile Library is opt-in and route-scoped. For v1 we need deterministic selection, safe fallback, and clear signals for SRE and customers to verify whether a profile was applied for a given request. This PR is scoped to runtime behavior only; control plane resolution/compatibility checks are handled upstream (see related PRs). Design overview: - Input contract: router attaches quantization selection metadata to the request context (grpc metadata + internal request proto field). Runtime treats this as advisory and re-validates profile/model compatibility against the local model + GPU runtime capabilities. - Profile loading: new QuantProfileManager loads profile metadata via registry client (cached), then downloads artifact bundle (signed) to a local content-addressed cache. Artifacts are keyed by (profile_id, artifact_sha256) to guarantee determinism and avoid alias drift. - Deterministic application: on each request, runtime resolves outcome = {disabled|applied|fallback} with a single pass decision. If artifacts are missing/invalid/incompatible, runtime falls back to baseline precision for that model variant and records the reason code. No retry loops. - Runtime integration: ModelExecutor now accepts an optional QuantizationModeSpec derived from the profile. Kernel selection remains in kernel auto-selector; runtime passes a constrained spec and relies on kernel guardrails to reject unsupported mixes. - Observability: Adds counters and histograms for enablement outcome, artifact cache behavior, load latencies, and per-request annotations (logs + traces) including quant_profile_id and resolution outcome. Metrics are low-cardinality by design; profile_id is recorded in logs/traces but not as a metrics label. Metrics/events added: - Counter: runtime.quant_profile.requests_total{outcome=applied|fallback|disabled, reason=...} - Counter: runtime.quant_profile.artifact_fetch_total{result=success|error, source=cache|registry} - Histogram: runtime.quant_profile.artifact_fetch_latency_ms - Histogram: runtime.quant_profile.profile_resolve_latency_us - Gauge: runtime.quant_profile.cache_entries (debug-only, exported behind internal flag) - Structured event (json log): quant_profile_resolution with fields {request_id, route_id, model_id, model_variant, quant_profile_id, outcome, reason, artifact_sha256} - Trace attribute: redwood.quant_profile.id, redwood.quant_profile.outcome, redwood.quant_profile.reason Safety/guardrails: - Default behavior unchanged when routing metadata is absent or explicitly indicates "default". - Fallback is always baseline precision; never attempts to select an alternate quant profile in-runtime. - All profile fetches are rate-limited and cached; failures do not fail the request unless the request explicitly mandates a profile (not supported in v1; we treat all as best-effort). - Validates artifact signature + sha256 match before loading. - Adds circuit-breaker style suppression: repeated registry errors degrade to fallback without spamming registry. Testing: - Unit tests: profile parsing/validation, artifact cache keying, determinism invariants, reason code coverage. - Integration test: fake registry + runtime exec path ensures a quant_profile_id flows through request context -> applied -> annotated logs. - Perf smoke: decode path overhead measured to be <0.3% in microbench; artifact load occurs on first hit only. Rollout plan: This lands behind the existing feature gate in runtime config (QuantProfileRuntimeEnabled). When disabled, all new code paths short-circuit at the request boundary. Observability will be used in perf-canary and early beta routes to verify applied/fallback rates and to correlate latency/cost deltas. Related: - ENG-5816 runtime integration - ENG-5817 dashboards/metrics follow-up - pr-18427 policy compatibility guardrails (upstream) - pr-18445 control plane endpoints (upstream) Notes: This PR intentionally does not implement the global kill-switch (tracked separately). It also does not add profile_id as a metric label to avoid cardinality issues; profile granularity is available via logs/traces and audit events upstream.
commits: runtime: add QuantProfileManager with registry client + artifact cache
runtime: plumb quant profile selection metadata through request context
runtime: apply quant mode spec to model executor and guard fallback
obs: emit quant_profile_resolution structured log + trace attributes
metrics: add outcome counters + fetch latency histograms (low cardinality)
tests: add unit/integration coverage for artifact validation + determinism
docs(internal): add runbook snippet for locating quant_profile_id in traces
review_conversation: Hiro Tanaka (review): Can we ensure the quant spec we pass cannot trigger a mixed FP8/INT8 path on unsupported GPUs? Suggest explicitly constraining allowed kernel families in the spec instead of relying only on selector rejection.

Noah Patel (author): Updated QuantizationModeSpec to include allowed_kernel_families derived from profile + local GPU caps. Selector still validates, but runtime no longer proposes mixed modes when caps don’t include them.
Omar El-Sayed (review): Any interaction with KV cache layout? Specifically, does enabling INT8 weights change KV precision assumptions or cache keying?

Noah Patel (author): KV cache stays in the baseline path for v1 (same precision/layout). Quant profile only affects weights/compute mode. Added a comment + a unit test asserting KV cache keying ignores quant_profile_id to avoid cache fragmentation.
Logan Wright (review): Please don’t add quant_profile_id as a metrics label; cardinality will be unbounded. Can we keep it to logs/traces and add a stable reason taxonomy for metrics?
Noah Patel (author): Agreed. Metrics now label only outcome + reason (bounded enum). quant_profile_id is in structured logs + traces only.
Nadia Rahman (review): For cost attribution, can we guarantee every request logs the resolved outcome even when disabled? Otherwise we can’t compute enabled-rate from sampled traces.
Noah Patel (author): Added a lightweight counter emitted on every request (disabled/applied/fallback). Trace attrs remain sampled; logs are available on-demand by request_id.
Mateo Alvarez (review): Determinism: ensure we never resolve an alias at runtime. Must be pinned to an immutable profile_id + artifact hash.
Noah Patel (author): Runtime only accepts explicit profile_id + artifact_sha256. If metadata contains alias fields they are ignored; also added a safeguard that rejects missing sha256 and falls back.
Sofia Ivanova (review): The error path currently retries registry fetch twice. This could amplify load during an incident. Prefer single attempt + cache negative results briefly.
Noah Patel (author): Removed retries; added a 30s negative cache for registry errors (bounded) and a suppression counter.
ci_summary: Buildkite: runtime-unit-tests (pass), runtime-integration-tests (pass), lint (pass), bazel-build (pass), perf-smoke (pass). One transient failure in runtime-integration-tests on first run (timeout) resolved on rerun after reducing artifact download test payload size.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Mateo Alvarez
